title: PolicyRuleset
description: Schema for the parsed form of config/policy/*.toml (ADR-0012). Rules are DECLARATIVE, not code, so authorization is reviewable as a diff and testable without running the agent.

minor_changes: 1.1.0 (ADR-0034): a rule may carry constraints without a decision; such rules are evaluated in a pass of their own, before the deciding pass. A rule carrying neither a decision nor a constraint is now a schema error — under 1.0.0 it validated and did nothing.
compatibility.notes: Config schema: additionalProperties is FALSE throughout (ADR-0015). Changing rule EVALUATION ORDER is MAJOR even with no schema change — order determines which rule matches, and a reordering silently alters every decision. Evaluation is TWO PASSES (ADR-0034, 1.1.0): constraint rules first, all of them, regardless of position; then deciding rules, first match wins, top to bottom, with defaults.decision as the fallthrough. The DECIDING order is unchanged from 1.0.0, which is why this is MINOR and not MAJOR — a constraint rule can only stop a call, never turn a denial into an allowance, so no ruleset's decisions move.

decision.description: PINNED TO deny BY THE SCHEMA. Not a default that can be overridden — allow-by-default means a forgotten tool registration becomes an open door. If this ever needs to change it requires a superseding ADR, and the schema change makes that visible.

audit.description: Log allows AND denies. A log of refusals alone cannot reconstruct what the system actually did.

rule.description: TWO PASSES (ADR-0034). Pass 1: every CONSTRAINT rule — a rule with a limit and no decision — applies to every call its match selects, regardless of the rule's position; exceeding a limit produces on_exceeded and evaluation stops. Pass 2: DECIDING rules, evaluated top to bottom, FIRST MATCH WINS, falling through to defaults.decision. Constraints bound; they do not authorise.

name.description: Appears verbatim in the AuditRecord.rule_name, so it should read well in an incident review.

reason.description: Surfaced to the user on a denial and recorded in the audit log.

confirmation_scope.description: ONLY per_invocation is permitted. A session-wide 'yes to all' is how confirmation prompts become rubber stamps, which is the failure mode confirmation exists to avoid. The enum has one value on purpose.

max_calls_per_turn.description: Runaway containment. A tool-calling bug can loop; this bounds the blast radius and the bill.

Rule.$comment: ADR-0034 rule 4: a rule must decide or constrain. A rule with neither is a load error, not a rule that silently does nothing — that shape validated under 1.0.0 and is the defect ADR-0034 was written about.

Match.description: All present conditions must hold (AND). An absent condition is a wildcard.

any.description: Matches everything. Use only for a terminal containment rule.

tool.description: Exact ToolSpec name, or a `capability.*` prefix glob.

trust.description: Matches the EFFECTIVE turn trust — the minimum across all sources (trust-context.schema.json). `untrusted` is an alias for external_content, retained because it reads more clearly in a deny rule.

rule.name: writes from untrusted content are denied
rule.reason: ADR-0012: injected content must not reach a write tool.
